newsitem.title: CHINA: Rupiah management policy to remain, cenbank says.
newsitem.headline: Rupiah management policy to remain, cenbank says.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank will continue its policy of gradually depreciating the currency, C. Harinowo, monetary management director at Bank Indonesia, said on Tuesday.
"We are continuing our depreciation policy, we are still very consistent," Harinowo told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Bank Indonesia widened the rupiah's band against the U.S. dollar to 12 percent from eight percent on Friday in a pre-emptive move following currency volatility in the region.
Harinowo said that by widening the trading band, rather than allowing the currency to float, Indonesia could assess the effectiveness of a floating rate policy.
"By widening the band, we learn how to have a floating rate policy," he said.
"At the end of the day, maybe we are moving towards that kind of floating rate environment, but we haven't any indication now of when that should be."
Harinowo said Indonesia has not experienced the same kind of speculative attacks against its currency that have plagued Thailand and the Philippines.
"At this point, we don't see that much going on in the market. During the Thai crisis, there was not that much affect on our market," he said.
